title: ChatGPT as an AI L2 Teaching Support: A Case Study of an EFL Teacher
extended_summary:
This paper examines how ChatGPT can support second-language teaching, focusing on one English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teacher’s use of the tool over a seven-month period. The study asks how the teacher integrated ChatGPT into teaching, how effective it was for her instructional goals, how she learned to craft prompts, and how she checked the reliability of the AI’s outputs. The broader problem addressed is whether generative AI can function as practical teaching support in real language-learning contexts while avoiding inaccuracies and bias.

The intervention studied was the teacher’s ongoing use of the free version of ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) to assist with lesson planning, in-class implementation, and assessment. Data came from the teacher’s ChatGPT history, lesson plans that incorporated ChatGPT, and a semi-structured interview. The analysis used thematic analysis to categorize uses of the tool, including curriculum suggestions, activity generation, vocabulary support, real-time classroom Q&A, interactive language practice, text editing, automated grading, and self-assessment materials. A major emphasis of the paper is the teacher’s development of more effective prompt-crafting strategies over time, culminating in a five-step prompt framework.

The study took place in a private language school in Spain serving Spanish learners preparing for Cambridge English exams. The focal participant was one experienced EFL teacher, while her students were described as subsidiary participants spanning children ages 4–12, teenagers ages 12–18, and adults. The context was face-to-face language teaching in small groups across proficiency levels from A1 to C1. The paper reports that ChatGPT was especially useful for producing lower-complexity materials, expanding resources for younger learners, and supporting classroom engagement and feedback processes, though outputs for advanced learners were sometimes too superficial or off-target.

The main conclusions are that ChatGPT can be a valuable support tool for EFL teaching when used critically and skillfully, especially for lesson planning, classroom material generation, and some assessment functions. The authors stress that prompt crafting and critical evaluation of outputs are essential competencies for teachers. They also conclude that teachers must verify AI-generated content for reliability, bias, and pedagogical fit. Because the study is a single qualitative case, the authors present the findings as exploratory and useful for informing future larger-scale studies rather than as broadly generalizable evidence.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative single instrumental case study with clear methods and rich implementation detail, but it includes only one teacher, lacks experimental or quasi-experimental design, and reports no standardized outcome estimates. It meets limited credibility criteria appropriate to qualitative evidence but cannot support strong causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests useful and potentially meaningful benefits for teacher workload, classroom engagement, and literacy/language support, but impacts are mostly perception-based and unquantified, with at least one concrete limitation in writing-score accuracy. Overall impact is promising but unclear in magnitude and generalizability.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) used by an EFL teacher over seven months to support lesson planning, generate classroom materials, enable in-class question answering and interactive language practice, and assist with assessment and feedback in a private language school serving children, teenagers, and adults.
ChatGPT used to assess learner writing, generate rubrics, provide automated grading/feedback, and compare AI scoring of Cambridge-style B2 writing against official handbook-based scoring criteria.

ChatGPT used as a language-support tool for grammar, vocabulary, reading, writing, and sentence/text editing tasks, including generating exercises, model texts, vocabulary tables, and revision support for EFL learners.

finding.finding_summary: In this qualitative single-case study, the teacher reported that ChatGPT provided significant support for lesson planning, material generation, and some assessment tasks, reducing workload and saving time while broadening the range of resources she could prepare for different proficiency levels. Evidence comes from analysis of 68 ChatGPT-supported productions collected over seven months plus a post-interview; no quantitative effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported usefulness/productivity in lesson planning, material development, classroom implementation, and assessment support; qualitative thematic analysis of chat history, lesson plans, and interview

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that ChatGPT helped generate writing tasks, reading-comprehension activities, vocabulary materials, and writing feedback, and the teacher perceived these supports as helpful for student comprehension, vocabulary retention, and writing-related instruction. However, when ChatGPT scored a Cambridge FCE B2 essay, its ratings diverged from the official benchmark by 3 total points, indicating limitations in assessment accuracy despite utility for drafting and feedback support.
finding.measure: Teacher-observed literacy support in writing/reading activities; AI scoring accuracy against Cambridge FCE writing scale benchmark
finding.study_size: n=1 teacher; student counts not reported

finding.finding_summary: The teacher used ChatGPT for interactive language practice, simulated conversations, role-play, vocabulary development, and real-time Q&A, and reported increased participation and enthusiasm as well as better tailoring of materials for different EFL levels. These findings are based on teacher perceptions and implementation records rather than independent pre/post fluency measures, so impact on speaking proficiency remains suggestive rather than causally established.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported usefulness of ChatGPT for speaking/writing practice, role-play, vocabulary support, and classroom participation
finding.study_size: n=1 teacher; small groups averaging about 8 students, total not reported

finding.finding_summary: The teacher reported increased student participation, enthusiasm, and engagement when incorporating ChatGPT-supported activities, especially among adolescent learners who showed high willingness to use AI in class. These engagement findings are qualitative and observational, with no standardized engagement survey or effect size reported.
finding.measure: Observed participation, enthusiasm, and willingness to use AI in class

finding.finding_summary: A central qualitative finding is that effective use of ChatGPT required and appeared to foster prompt crafting, critical evaluation of outputs, cross-checking with sources, and collaborative review by students, the teacher, and colleagues. The paper frames these as important AI-related competencies and describes their development over the seven-month period, but does not quantify gains with validated instruments.
finding.measure: Qualitative evidence of prompt-crafting skill, critical thinking, source verification, and collaborative review practices
